source.title: Bataan-Cavite Interlink Bridge Project — Final Updated Environmental Impact Assessment Report
source.provider: Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank; Department of Public Works and Highways project; prepared by T.Y. Lin International–Pyunghwa Engineering Consultants joint venture
sections: Section 8.1.2.2 Livelihoods, printed pages 8-19 to 8-21 (Naic fisheries interviews and catch context)

access.status: Relevant full-text sections reviewed through the official AIIB-hosted PDF web view on 2026-10-31; PDF not downloaded or retained locally.

fieldStudy.surveyWindow: The report says stream surveys were conducted during 2021 and 2022; it does not give fish-specific observation/catch dates in these summaries.
fieldStudy.surveySelection: Four Cavite watercourses were covered: Labac River (one ecology station), Timbugan Creek (one), Timalan River main stem (six), and the unnamed Timalan west branch (one). Selection was based on proximity to project works and potential project impacts; this is not a province-wide fish inventory.
fieldStudy.fishEvidenceMethod: The stream-ecology methods describe observation of local fishing activity and discussions with locals about fish species, abundance, and catch effort. They do not describe standardized fish capture or identification protocols, specimen vouchers, or a taxon-by-station fish table.
fieldStudy.spatialLimits: The ecology station map is visual project context. No station coordinates or validated channel/waterbody geometry were adopted from it.
fieldStudy.salinityLimits: The report describes longitudinal freshwater-to-estuarine conditions in the Timalan main stem and mostly estuarine conditions in Timbugan Creek. These are source-era segment descriptions, not a current or whole-waterbody classification.

waterbodyReviews.sourceLocation: Labac River fish-and-fishing summary; one ecology station for the river

sourceReportedFishLabels.name: Oreochromis niloticus
sourceReportedFishLabels.reportedContext: Named as a fish used for subsistence fishing. The report does not identify the fish observation/catch station or date.

sourceReportedFishLabels.name: Mugil cephalus
sourceReportedFishLabels.reportedContext: Named as a fish used for subsistence fishing. The report does not identify the fish observation/catch station or date.

waterbodyReviews.interpretation: Historical EIA fishery-context leads only; not station-dated occurrences, standardized sampling results, a complete checklist, or current presence. The report says mangrove areas may mean its fish diversity summary is incomplete.

waterbodyReviews.sourceLocation: One surveyed lower segment of Timbugan Creek
waterbodyReviews.surveyObservation: The report says no fish or fishing were observed and no fishing activity was reported in the surveyed segment; it says upstream segments were not surveyed.
waterbodyReviews.interpretation: A bounded non-observation for one surveyed segment, not evidence that fish are absent from Timbugan Creek or its upstream reaches. The source-era low dissolved oxygen value is not a current water-safety or fishing advisory.

waterbodyReviews.sourceLocation: Timalan River main stem; six ecology stations, but no fish-name allocation by station

sourceReportedFishLabels.name: Glossogobius giuris
sourceReportedFishLabels.taxonomyStatus: Source spelling preserved; independent nomenclature and field identification not verified in this review.

waterbodyReviews.rankCheck: Although the EIA calls these five fish species, two labels are family-level groups; only three are binomial species names.
waterbodyReviews.interpretation: Source-reported-or-observed main-stem leads only. Do not allocate all names to each station or to the west branch. The report's native/introduced summary is not adopted because the family-level groups are unresolved.

waterbodyReviews.sourceLocation: One station on the unnamed west branch
waterbodyReviews.surveyObservation: The report says no fish or fishing activity was documented at or near the selected location.
waterbodyReviews.interpretation: A bounded point/segment non-observation only; it is not evidence of fish absence from the branch or main stem.

rightsReview.decision: Keep the summary as minimal, attributed research documentation. Do not reproduce report prose, tables, maps, or images; no public species projection is approved.

nextAction: Keep the February 2020 Naic interview catch list separate from the Timalan River main-stem fish summary. If considering Corregidor/Caballo marine-area research entries, first resolve species-specific grounds, name spellings, identification support and reuse terms; continue seeking station-resolved, reusable freshwater evidence for Timalan and Naic.

naicOffshoreFisheryContext.sourceSection: Section 8.1.2.2 Livelihoods, printed pages 8-19 to 8-21 (Naic fisheries interviews and catch context)
naicOffshoreFisheryContext.reportedFishingGrounds: Waters around Corregidor and Caballo Islands; the report says Naic fisherfolk commonly travel beyond official municipal fishing grounds.
naicOffshoreFisheryContext.taxonomicHandling: Source spellings are retained verbatim in this interview-context review; no independent taxonomic validation or correction was performed. In particular, the report prints Ratrilliger brachysoma.
naicOffshoreFisheryContext.waterbodyAttribution: Not assigned to Timalan River, its estuary, or a particular marine waterbody. The report names the fishers’ home barangays and describes fishing grounds around Corregidor and Caballo; it does not give species-specific capture coordinates or a route crosswalk.
naicOffshoreFisheryContext.separationFromRiverEcology: Keep distinct from Exhibit 6-14, which separately reports or observes five fish labels in the Timalan River main stem without station allocation. Oyster farming is described along the Timalan estuary, but that does not relocate the interview catch list to the river.
limits: The fish list is source-reported interview catch context, not a standardized specimen or occurrence dataset.
No species-specific catch date, capture coordinates, station, voucher, or field identification protocol is given.
This source does not establish current presence, abundance, local catchability, diet, or a complete Manila Bay/Corregidor inventory.
No species records are assigned to a waterbody and no public-app projection is approved; item-specific reuse terms remain unverified.
